featureRef: 30.2 Working and closing a parent complaint
name: Take an open parent complaint, work it, and close it on an outcome the family has seen
priorityReason: A complaint raised and never worked is worse than one never raised, and this is where it is worked.

goal.actor: the desk, and above it the School Admin and the Principal
goal.capability: to take a complaint up, work it, and close it on a recorded outcome
goal.outcome: the family is told what was done, and a complaint about somebody is not handled by that somebody

secondaryActors.involvement: Takes over any complaint the desk cannot resolve, and holds a reopened one.
Holds the complaints that route directly to them, and can read the rest.
Holds a complaint that names the Principal.
Is told the outcome and confirms it.

additional.description: A complaint is raised and enters the queue.
A parent does not accept the outcome and reopens the complaint (BR-6).

preconditions.condition: An authenticated session exists and the acting user is on the desk, or above it.
The acting user is not a colleague of the person the complaint names (BR-4).

postConditions: The complaint was taken up and worked, with every action recorded against it.
A complaint the desk could not resolve was redirected to the School Admin.
A complaint naming a role routed above that role rather than to it.
Who could read the complaint was scoped, so a complaint about a named teacher was not visible to that teacher.
Where the desk staff member was a colleague of the person named, the complaint was not routed through them.
The outcome was recorded and the parent was told.
The parent confirmed the outcome. Where they did not accept it, the complaint was reopened once and is now held by the School Admin.
A harm allegation was not closed by this route at all.

dataFields.name: Complaint
dataFields.validation: An open complaint in the queue.

dataFields.name: Held by
dataFields.validation: Who currently holds it. The parent is told throughout (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Action recorded
dataFields.validation: 10 to 2000 characters. Every action taken is recorded against the complaint (BR-1).
dataFields.example: Spoke to the transport contractor and reviewed the route timings for the month.

dataFields.name: Names a role
dataFields.validation: Where the complaint names the School Admin or the Principal, it routes above that role rather than to it (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Redirect reason
dataFields.validation: 20 to 500 characters. Required when the desk redirects to the School Admin (BR-2).
dataFields.example: This concerns the transport contract, which the desk cannot change.

dataFields.name: Outcome
dataFields.validation: 20 to 2000 characters. What was done. The parent is told it (BR-5).
dataFields.example: The contractor has been put on notice and the route timing revised from Monday.

dataFields.name: Parent confirmed
dataFields.validation: Whether the parent accepted the outcome (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Reopened
dataFields.validation: Set where the parent did not accept the outcome. Once only, and it is then held by the School Admin (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Days open
dataFields.validation: How long the complaint has been open.

entities.notes: Its holder, outcome and status move. Never deleted.
One row per action taken, with who and when. Append only (BR-1).
One row per redirect, with the reason and who redirected it (BR-2).
Who may read the complaint. Scoped so it is not visible to the person it names (BR-4).
Every action, redirect, outcome and closure.

permissions.rowScope: Own branch, ordinary complaints not naming them or a colleague.
permissions.notes: Takes the complaint up, works it and closes it. Never sees a harm allegation (BR-4, BR-8).
Takes over any complaint the desk cannot resolve, and holds a reopened one. Does not hold a complaint naming them (BR-2, BR-3).
Holds the complaints that route directly to them, including any naming the School Admin, and can read the rest.
Holds a complaint that names the Principal (BR-3).
Is told the outcome, confirms it, and may reopen once (BR-6).

permissions.rowScope: No access. A complaint naming a teacher is not visible to that teacher (BR-4).

businessRules.rule: The staff member on the desk takes the complaint up and works it, with every action recorded against it.
A complaint the desk cannot resolve is redirected to the School Admin, who takes it from there. This is an alternate route within working the complaint rather than a separate thing.

A complaint that names a role routes above that role rather than to it. A complaint about the School Admin does not go to the School Admin; it goes to the Principal. A complaint about the Principal goes to the Super Admin.

Who may read a complaint is scoped. A parent complaining about a named teacher does not have that complaint visible to the teacher, and where the desk staff member is a colleague of the person named the complaint is not routed through them.
The outcome is recorded and the parent is told.
The parent confirms the outcome. A complaint closed on an outcome the family does not accept can be reopened once, and is then held by the School Admin.
A complaint alleging that a child has been harmed is not closed by this route at all. It is held by the Principal and read only by those the Principal permits.
Every action recorded against the complaint stays. Nothing is edited or removed, so the record of how a complaint was handled is a record.
A complaint can be reopened once. A second refusal to accept the outcome does not reopen it again; it stays with the School Admin.
The parent is told who holds the complaint at every stage, so a redirect does not look like silence.

transitions.condition: It names the School Admin or the Principal and routes above that role (BR-3).
The desk cannot resolve it and redirects it to the School Admin, with a reason (BR-2).
The School Admin takes it from there.
The outcome is recorded and the parent is told (BR-5).
The parent confirms the outcome (BR-6, BR-7).
The parent does not accept it. Reopened once, and held by the School Admin (BR-6, BR-10).
Closed after the second outcome. It cannot be reopened again (BR-10).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Help Desk → Complaints → Take up
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses where the acting user is the person named or a colleague of them, and tells the parent who holds it.

basicFlow.navigation: Work the complaint → Record an action
basicFlow.userAction: Works the complaint, recording every action taken against it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Appends the action. Nothing is edited or removed afterwards.

basicFlow.navigation: Work the complaint → Redirect to the School Admin
basicFlow.userAction: Redirects a complaint the desk cannot resolve, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Passes it to the School Admin and tells the parent who now holds it.
Routes a complaint naming the School Admin to the Principal, and one naming the Principal to the Super Admin.
Scopes who may read it, so a complaint about a named teacher is not visible to that teacher and is not routed through a colleague of theirs.

basicFlow.navigation: Work the complaint → Record the outcome
basicFlow.userAction: Records the outcome and tells the parent.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records it and sends it to the parent.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Portal → My complaints → Confirm the outcome
basicFlow.systemResponse: Closes the complaint, or reopens it once where the parent does not accept it.
Closes the complaint. A harm allegation is not closed by this route at all.

alternateFlows.condition: The desk cannot resolve the complaint
alternateFlows.navigation: Work the complaint → Redirect to the School Admin
alternateFlows.behaviour: It goes to the School Admin, who takes it from there. This is a route within working the complaint (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The complaint names the School Admin
alternateFlows.behaviour: It routes to the Principal rather than to the School Admin, since a complaint about somebody is not handled by that somebody (BR-3).
It routes to the Super Admin on the same principle (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The desk staff member is a colleague of the person named
alternateFlows.behaviour: The complaint is not routed through them and goes to somebody else (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The parent does not accept the outcome
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is reopened once and is then held by the School Admin. A second refusal does not reopen it again (BR-6, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The complaint is a harm allegation
alternateFlows.navigation: Help Desk → Complaints held by the Principal
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is not closed by this route at all. It is held by the Principal and read only by those they permit (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: A teacher is named in the complaint
alternateFlows.behaviour: The complaint is not visible to that teacher at any point (BR-4).

openQuestions.question: This routes a complaint about a teacher, a fee or a bus through the same desk that fixes system faults. Whether the person on the IT desk is the right first stop for a non-technical complaint, or whether complaints need a front-office role of their own, needs deciding.
openQuestions.assumption: Modelled through the desk, per the document, but flagged there as needing a decision.

openQuestions.question: How does the system know a complaint names a particular person or role, given the parent writes free text?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The routing rule depends on it.

openQuestions.question: What is a colleague, for the purpose of not routing a complaint through one?
openQuestions.assumption: Not defined, and the rule depends on it.

openQuestions.question: Is there a time limit within which a complaint must be taken up or resolved?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. Days open is shown but nothing acts on it.

openQuestions.question: What happens where the parent never confirms the outcome?
openQuestions.assumption: It stays awaiting confirmation as modelled and is surfaced, but never closes.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
